transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Arielle Gomez (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Ironbridge - Head of Vendor Risk), Lena Ortiz (Ironbridge - Security Engineer), Markus Chen (Procurement), Hannah Liu (Legal)

Summary: walkthrough of Standardized Information Gathering (SIG) questionnaire and CAIQ items, clarification on SOC 2 / ISO artifacts, RBAC/SSO, audit log retention and delivery, data residency options, and encryption (KMS/BYOK). Agreed to share evidence links and schedule a deeper KMS and audit-logs technical deep-dive.

Topics covered: SIG/CAIQ mapping, SOC 2 type II evidence, ISO27001 status, SSO/SAML and RBAC integration, audit logs (retention/format/export), data residency and VPC/private deployment options, encryption at rest and customer-managed keys (BYOK), evidence packet and timeline.

Transcript (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect):
00:00 - Arielle: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll go through the SIG spreadsheet and mark any questions you want clarified, i have diego and priya from engineering to cover the deep stuff
00:12 - Samir: thanks ariell, yes we just want to understand how you map controls to your SOC 2 and where we can get evidence, also looking at KMS, BYOK, and VPC separation for regulated data
00:28 - Diego: sure, quick note, Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report is available, i'll ping the link in chat — it's the latest 2025-12-31 period, and we also have an ISO27001 statement, not sure if you got the cover letter yet
00:45 - Lena: can you confirm retention of audit logs? we need 12 months easily searchable, also chain of custody for log exports
01:05 - Priya: right now our hosted offering retains logs for 90 days by default, but for Dedicated/Private customers we can extend retention and provide exports to your S3, or a syslog endpoint, and we support on-request retention for audits. there was a small typo in the spreadsheet where 'log export' row referenced 'k-v cache' — ignore that, it's a transcribe glitch
01:30 - Markus: procurement question — is there a data residency guarantee? we operate in EU and US, need to ensure customer data remains in-region
01:45 - Arielle: yes we have region-specific endpoints and can pin workloads to eu-west and us-east, for Private deployments you can run in your VPC; we'll document that in the SIG answers.
02:02 - Samir: ok on encryption, specifically do you support customer-managed keys, HSM integration, and can we tie it to our KMS?
02:17 - Diego: we support BYOK for Private and Dedicated via customer-managed KMS. the hosted product supports envelope encryption with provider-managed keys by default; for enterprise contracts we enable CMKs bound to the customer's KMS (AWS KMS / GCP CMEK), and we have HSM-backed options for import. I'll prepare an architecture diagram.
02:45 - Hannah: legal wants to see key lifecycle and proof-of-destruction process if we terminate, any SI signs?
02:54 - Priya: yes, we maintain key rotation policies and documented key deletion procedures; for BYOK, key material never leaves customer's KMS, Redwood holds only wrapped keys. we'll provide the KMS integration doc as evidence.
03:20 - Lena: about RBAC and SSO — do you support SAML with SCIM provisioning and fine-grained roles? we need auditability of who invoked model endpoints
03:38 - Diego: we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning for users, and RBAC that maps to API key scopes and console roles. For programmatic calls we log token usage and map to principal IDs; we can provide logs showing user/principal, IP, request path, and model served.
04:05 - Samir: there are some sig control rows around 'third party data processing' and 'subprocessor list' — how do you handle subprocessors and notification?
04:20 - Arielle: we maintain a subprocessor registry, we'll share a current list (SaaS infra providers, CDN, monitoring) and we notify customers on material changes. for Dedicated we can optionally restrict some subprocessors.
04:35 - Markus: procurement will need SLA and termination clauses, and evidence of penetration testing and remediation timelines
04:48 - Priya: we run annual external pentests and quarterly internal scans; remediation windows depend on severity but criticals get a 30-day SLA typically. we can include pentest summary and remediation tickets in the evidence packet (redacted).
05:10 - Lena: audit logs format — can you provide JSON syslog exports and an example schema? our SIEM ingests JSON, would prefer structured events
05:26 - Diego: yes we can export JSON structured logs that include timestamp, tenant_id, request_id, user_principal, model_version, tokens_in/tokens_out, latency_ms. sample log export will be attached. note: in hosted mode we sanitize PII by default on logs unless you opt in for enhanced logging for debugging
05:56 - Samir: any compliance certifications besides SOC2 and ISO? we need PCI scoping guidance, we're not expecting you to be PCI certified but want PSPR guidance
06:12 - Arielle: we're not PCI certified at org-level, but we provide guidance for PCI scope reduction and options for Private deployment to keep cardholder data off Redwood systems; we'll call out recommended architecture patterns in the answers
06:30 - Hannah: on legal side, we'd like to see encryption at rest and in transit statements plus attestation for key handling; also concerned about subpoena and e-discovery — do you have a TAM?
06:48 - Priya: we encrypt all data in transit (TLS 1.2/1.3) and at rest using AES-256. For BYOK customers, Redwoods (transcription error: Redwood's) don't have access to plaintext. Subpoena/requests follow our data access policy and we provide a process doc; we'll add that doc to the evidence bundle.
07:15 - Markus: how do you handle data deletion requests and can you prove deletion for a given tenant?
07:25 - Diego: we support tenant-scoped deletion; for Dedicated/Private we can run deletion jobs and provide signed deletion certificates. on hosted we follow documented retention and deletion workflows and can provide logs of deletion operations.
07:52 - Arielle: ok let's walk the SIG spreadsheet by section — i'll share my screen and mark high priority items, but i'll call out a few rows where we often see redlines: CA-2/CA-3 equivalent rows about change control and secure code reviews, also CR-8 on third-party assessment
08:10 - (screen share noise / minor crosstalk)
08:30 - Diego: quick clarification: on the CAIQ 'data residency' row we put 'region pinning available' but that is for Dedicated and Private; hosted has region selection but not absolute guaranteed geo-fencing unless contract-specified. please flag if you need contract language.
09:00 - Samir: we'll need contract language; ironbridge requires contractual guarantee for EU-only residency for some regulated workloads
09:12 - Arielle: noted, we'll push that as a redline to the legal team and propose clause examples.
09:24 - Lena: for evidence, what's easiest — do you prefer a single zip with PDFs or a shared folder with links?
09:33 - Priya: shared folder with links is easiest for iterative updates; we'll provide a manifest CSV mapping SIG questions to evidence files and links.
09:44 - Markus: the customer security questionnaire also asks about availability targets, what's your SLA?
09:52 - Arielle: for Dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets (we'll paste the SLA language); hosted has standard uptime with best-effort and available premium SLA as an add-on.
10:05 - Samir: ok next, can you expand on how you do model validation and regression detection — we need to know if there's potential leakage or prompts being cached across tenants
10:20 - Diego: we isolate model contexts per-tenant; the KV cache is tenant-scoped; prefix caching is configurable and not shared. we have monitoring that detects drift/regression; we can run eval suites on your prompt sets as part of Redwood Optimize. note: occasional speech glitch - 'kv cache' was transcribed as 'k v cash' in the spreadsheet comments
10:50 - Lena: for logging of model outputs, do you retain actual user prompts in logs? that's a sensitive area
11:00 - Priya: we sanitize PII in logs by default; retention of raw prompts for debugging is by opt-in and subject to stricter retention and access controls; we'll call out who in Redwood can access debug logs and we enforce RBAC and approval flows.
11:20 - Samir: on RBAC, can roles be scoped to environment, model, and API key? we need principle of least privilege
11:30 - Diego: yes roles can be scoped; API keys can be limited to route/model/usage; console roles are separate. we also support audit-able approvals for elevated operations.
12:00 - Hannah: one of the sig questions is about encryption key escrow and escrow policies — do you offer escrow for keys?
12:12 - Priya: we don't escrow customer key material; BYOK means customer retains control. we can integrate with your KMS provider for dual control patterns if needed.
12:34 - Markus: procurement will request a copy of the pentest report redacted, and SOC 2 — are those available asap?
12:45 - Arielle: yes SOC 2 Type II and pentest summaries will be uploaded, full pentest may be redacted. sending today's answers and evidence pack by Monday.
13:05 - Samir: great, last question on subprocessor notification cadence and exit conditions — how quickly will you notify if a new subprocessor is engaged?
13:20 - Arielle: we notify customers 30 days prior for material subprocessors; for non-material we provide quarterly updates. we'll include the subprocessor registry link.
13:45 - (Customer asks a few clarifying quick questions; some timestamps omitted)
40:30 - Arielle: recap — we'll send completed SIG/CAIQ answers, SOC 2 Type II report link, pentest summary, KMS integration doc, sample audit log export, and subprocessor registry. Diego will follow up with a KMS/BYOK deep-dive and sample architecture.
41:00 - Samir: sounds good, please include any contract language for EU-only residency and extended log retention options
41:12 - Arielle: noted. we'll aim to have the initial evidence bundle by 2026-05-18 and schedule the deep-dive week of 2026-05-25, i'll send a calendar invite after the call.
41:30 - (closing pleasantries)
41:45 - End of recording

References / links mentioned: https://redwood.example.com/evidence/CRM-42389 (SIG answers and evidence bundle - placeholder), SOC2 report link (sent in chat), subprocessor registry link (to be shared).

Notes on transcription errors: some product names and technical terms mis-transcribed (e.g., 'k v cache' vs 'KV cache', 'Redwood's' sometimes written as 'Redwood' or 'Redwoody' in audio), speaker labels approximate.

Final recap / Next steps (text): Arielle to upload SIG answers and evidence (SOC2, pentest summary, KMS doc) by 2026-05-18; Diego to prepare KMS/BYOK architecture and sample audit log exports for deep-dive by 2026-05-22; Customer (Samir) to provide Ironbridge control set and data residency constraints by 2026-05-20.
